+Nuxt also provides a [`<NuxtErrorBoundary>`](/docs/api/components/nuxt-error-boundary) component that allows you to handle errors within your app, without replacing your entire site with an error page.

-This component is responsible for handling errors that occur within its default slot. On client-side, it will prevent the error from bubbling up to the top level, and will render the `#error` slot instead.

+This component is responsible for handling errors that occur within its default slot. It will prevent the error from bubbling up to the top level, and will render the `#error` slot instead. This applies both on the client and during server-side rendering: if content inside the boundary throws on the server, the `#error` slot is rendered in the HTML response (with a `200` status) and the client hydrates into the same state.

+The boundary catches everything thrown while rendering its default slot, including errors created with `fatal: true`. It does not intercept errors that bypass the component tree: calling [`showError`](/docs/api/utils/show-error) directly, errors thrown in route middleware or during navigation (such as a 404 for an unmatched route), or `useFetch`/`useAsyncData` failures, which are returned in `error` rather than thrown. A default slot rendered by a vapor component is only caught on the client.
+Server-side catching is controlled by the [`experimental.ssrErrorBoundary`](/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#ssrerrorboundary) option, which is enabled by default.

The `#error` slot will receive `error` as a prop. (If you set `error = null` it will trigger re-rendering the default slot; you'll need to ensure that the error is fully resolved first or the error slot will just be rendered a second time.)

- **Client-side payload extraction**: [`experimental.payloadExtraction`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#payload-extraction-defaults-to-client) is `'client'`, inlining the payload in the HTML of a prerendered page

- **`clearNuxtState` resets to defaults**: `clearNuxtState` [resets state to its initial value](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#respect-defaults-when-clearing-usestate) instead of setting it to `undefined`
- **Early return from `navigateTo`**: A successful top-level `await navigateTo()` [stops the rest of your `setup()` running](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#early-return-from-navigateto)

+- **Server-side error boundaries**: `<NuxtErrorBoundary>` [catches errors thrown while server-rendering its default slot](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#nuxterrorboundary-catches-server-side-errors) instead of letting them reach the error page
- **Non-async `callHook`**: [`callHook` may return `void`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#non-async-callhook) instead of always returning a `Promise`

- **Comment node placeholders**: Client-only components use [comment nodes instead of `<div>`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#client-only-comment-placeholders) as SSR placeholders, fixing a scoped styles hydration issue
- **Server auto-imports off**: Server code [imports Nitro's helpers explicitly](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#server-auto-imports-are-now-opt-in) rather than relying on the auto-import layer

+`experimental.ssrErrorBoundary` is now enabled by default. When content inside a [`<NuxtErrorBoundary>`](/docs/api/components/nuxt-error-boundary) throws during server-side rendering, the boundary renders its `#error` slot in the HTML response with a `200` status, and the client hydrates into the same state. Previously the error escaped to the full-screen error page, with the error's status code.

+This includes errors created with `createError({ status: 404 })` in a page's `setup`: if `<NuxtPage>` or a layout's `<slot />` is wrapped in a boundary, such a page now responds with `200` and the boundary's `#error` slot.
+`<NuxtClientFallback>` and `experimental.clientFallback` are deprecated in favour of `<NuxtErrorBoundary retry-on-client>`.

+If a page relies on throwing an error to respond with the error page and its status code, move the boundary so that it does not wrap the page, or call [`showError`](/docs/api/utils/show-error) instead of throwing. To keep the previous behaviour:

Nuxt provides the `<NuxtClientFallback>` component to render its content on the client if any of its children trigger an error in SSR.

+`<NuxtClientFallback>` is deprecated. [`<NuxtErrorBoundary>`](/docs/api/components/nuxt-error-boundary) now catches server-side errors too, and its `retry-on-client` prop provides the same "try again on the client" behaviour, with the error available in the `#error` slot.

-description: The <NuxtErrorBoundary> component handles client-side errors happening in its default slot.
+description: The <NuxtErrorBoundary> component handles errors happening in its default slot, on the server and on the client.
The `<NuxtErrorBoundary>` uses Vue's [`onErrorCaptured`](https://vuejs.org/api/composition-api-lifecycle#onerrorcaptured) hook under the hood.

+When content in the default slot throws, the `#error` slot is rendered in its place. This works during server-side rendering as well as on the client: a server-side error results in the `#error` slot being part of the HTML response (with a `200` status), and the error is passed to the client so that it hydrates into the same state. Calling `clearError` on the client then re-renders the default slot.

+In production, a server-side error that is not an HTTP error (such as one created with [`createError`](/docs/api/utils/create-error)) reaches the `#error` slot as a generic `500` error, so its message and data are not sent to the browser. HTTP errors keep their `status`, `message` and `data`.

+Server-side catching is controlled by the [`experimental.ssrErrorBoundary`](/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#ssrerrorboundary) option, which is enabled by default. When disabled, the boundary only catches client-side errors.

+The boundary catches everything thrown while rendering its default slot, including errors created with `fatal: true`. It does not intercept errors that bypass the component tree, such as calls to [`showError`](/docs/api/utils/show-error), errors thrown in route middleware, or `useFetch`/`useAsyncData` failures (which are returned in `error` rather than thrown). A default slot rendered by a vapor component is only caught on the client.

+- `retryOnClient`: When the error was caught during server-side rendering, re-render the default slot on the client once mounted. Use this for content that only fails on the server (for example, a component that accesses `window`): the `#error` slot is served in the HTML, then replaced by the real content in the browser. If the default slot throws on the client as well, the `#error` slot is rendered again with the client-side error.
-- `@error`: Event emitted when the default slot of the component throws an error.
+- `@error`: Event emitted when the default slot of the component throws an error. For an error caught during server-side rendering, it is emitted on the server only.
